$$|\mathcal T_U|=2B_{11}.$$
If such a triple’s tile is full, its missing corner is an endpoint of a different original source. That foreign source can have only one endpoint in the tile: the other three corners already belong to the triple owner.Its singleton profile is therefore either  $1P1T$  or  $1P2T$ . These are exactly the contacts counted by  $B_U$  and  $F_U$ . Hence there is a disjoint partition
$$\mathcal T_U
=
\mathcal T_U^{\mathrm{unfilled}}
\;\dot\cup\;
\mathcal T_U^{\mathrm{full,irregular}}
\;\dot\cup\;
\mathcal T_U^{\mathrm{full,regular}},$$
and
$$\boxed{U_0=2B_{11}-B_U-F_U.}$$
A physical tile cannot contain two original triple owners, so counting these full contacts by physical tile or by original triple occurrence gives the same total.2.2 Activated zero-rotor singletonsLet  $\mathcal T_Z$  be the original zero-rotor triple occurrences, and  $\mathcal S_Z$  their paired original regular singleton occurrences. The established pairing is a bijection
$$\phi:\mathcal T_Z\longrightarrow\mathcal S_Z.$$

$$\phi(\mathcal T_Z^{\mathrm{full}})
\subseteq
\mathcal S_Z^{\mathrm{act}}.$$

$$\mathcal S_Z^{\mathrm{act}}
=
\phi(\mathcal T_Z^{\mathrm{full}})
\;\dot\cup\;
\{s\in\mathcal S_Z^{\mathrm{act}}:

The filled triples split into  $B_R$  and  $F_R$ , so
$$D_R=B_R+F_R+Z_0,$$
or equivalently,
$$\boxed{Z_0=D_R-B_R-F_R.}$$

}$$

R=0

$$J=A+U_0+Z_0+L_1+L_3.$$
Then
$$2R=J+2L_{2\mathrm{bar}}+2L_{2\mathrm{mutual}},$$
so  $J$  is even and
$$R=L_{2\mathrm{bar}}+L_{2\mathrm{mutual}}+\frac J2.$$

$$\sigma\ge
N-G+L_{2\mathrm{bar}}+L_{2\mathrm{mutual}}
+\frac{A+U_0+Z_0+L_1+L_3}{2}.$$
The reserve expression is exact; the statement about ambient  $\sigma$  remains a lower bound, as it should.4.3 Allocation and failure equivalencesThe original sufficient joint allocation is
$$2G+B_U+B_R\le2N+2B_{11}+\Lambda.$$
Using the half-slot identity, this is equivalent to
$$G\le N+R,$$
and therefore to
$$\boxed{2G\le2N+A+U_0+Z_0+H.}$$
Failure means  $N+R-G<0$ . Since that expression is an integer,
$$R\le G-N-1.$$
Thus failure is equivalent to
$$\boxed{A+U_0+Z_0+H\le2G-2N-2.}$$
The subtraction by two is justified. It does not require any separate parity hypothesis on an individual defect count.The text also correctly distinguishes failure of this allocation from failure of the ambient grid inequality. A negative lower bound for  $\sigma$  supplies no negative upper bound for  $\sigma$ .5. $$d_Q=f_Q=0,\qquad \Lambda_Q\ge1.$$
Hence the new local identity gives
$$h_Q=\Lambda_Q\ge1.$$

$$G_b\le H.$$

This is one substitution into the exact reserve decomposition. It does not add a second blank-gate charge or reuse the regular-event credit.6. The single-positive conditional theorem is valid for unrestricted permitted widthFor  $N=1$ , the established two-side count gives  $G\le2$ , while the exact identity gives  $R\ge0$ .Failure of the joint allocation requires
$$1+R-G<0.$$
Consequently,
$$G=2,\qquad R=0.$$
The seven-term equivalence then forces every listed count to vanish. In particular: $U_0=0$ : every original phase11 U triple tile is full. $Z_0=0$ : every activated zero-rotor singleton has a full paired triple tile. $L_3=0$ : there is no mixed nonfull three-endpoint tile. $H=0$ , together with  $G_b\le H$ : both marked gates are occupied. $A=0$ : both original positive terminal singleton occurrences are unactivated.The established universal phase10 activation theorem excludes a phase10 owner at either occupied gate. $$A+U_0+Z_0+H>0.$$
This sum equals the even integer  $2R$ , so it is at least two. Therefore  $R\ge1$ , and
$$N+R-G=1+R-G\ge0.$$
This proves the joint allocation, and hence the coefficient-one conclusion through the ledger, whenever a defect occurs.
